text: After the death of Joshua, the Israelites asked the LORD, "Which of us is to go up first against the Canaanites to fight them?"
The LORD answered, "Judah is to go up. I have handed the land over to him."

Then Judah said to his brother Simeon, "Come up with me into the territory allotted to me, and let us fight the Canaanites together; then I will go with you into your territory." So Simeon went with him.
Judah went up, and the LORD handed the Canaanites and the Perizzites over to them; they struck down ten thousand men at Bezek.
At Bezek they came upon Adoni-bezek and fought him, and they defeated the Canaanites and the Perizzites.
Adoni-bezek fled, but they pursued him, captured him, and cut off his thumbs and big toes.

Then Adoni-bezek said, "Seventy kings with their thumbs and big toes cut off used to pick up scraps under my table. As I have done, so God has repaid me." They brought him to Jerusalem, and there he died.

versions.text: Then Adoni-bezek said, "Seventy kings with their thumbs and big toes cut off used to scavenge under my table. As I have done, so God has repaid me." They brought him to Jerusalem, and there he died.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew מְלַקְּטִים means to gather up scraps; "scavenge" is an odd, harsh word choice for oral reading and slightly shifts the sense.

text: The men of Judah fought against Jerusalem and captured it. They put its people to the sword and set the city on fire.
After that, the men of Judah went down to fight the Canaanites who lived in the hill country, in the Negev, and in the foothills.
Judah marched against the Canaanites living in Hebron—Hebron was formerly called Kiriath-arba—and they defeated Sheshai, Ahiman, and Talmai.
From there they advanced against the inhabitants of Debir, which was formerly called Kiriath-sepher.
Caleb said, "Whoever attacks Kiriath-sepher and takes it, I will give him my daughter Achsah in marriage."
Othniel son of Kenaz, Caleb's younger brother, took it, so Caleb gave him his daughter Achsah in marriage.
When she came to Othniel, she urged him to ask her father for a field. As she got down from her donkey, Caleb asked her, "What do you want?"
She answered, "Grant me a favor. Since you have given me land in the Negev, give me springs of water as well." So Caleb gave her the upper and lower springs.

The descendants of Moses' father-in-law, the Kenite, went up with the people of Judah from the City of Palms to the wilderness of Judah, which lies in the Negev near Arad, and they went and settled among the people there.

Judah went with his brother Simeon, and together they defeated the Canaanites living in Zephath. They devoted the city to destruction, and so it was named Hormah.<note>Hormah sounds like the Hebrew word for "destruction."</note>

versions.text: Judah went with his brother Simeon, and together they defeated the Canaanites living in Zephath. They devoted the city to destruction, and so it was named Hormah.
versions.explanation: The wordplay between "devoted to destruction" (herem) and the name Hormah is invisible to English hearers; a brief footnote would clarify why the name follows from the action.

text: Judah also took Gaza with its territory, Ashkelon with its territory, and Ekron with its territory.
The LORD was with Judah, and they took possession of the hill country, but they could not drive out the people of the plain, because they had iron chariots.
Hebron was given to Caleb, as Moses had promised, and he drove out from there the three sons of Anak.
But the Benjaminites did not drive out the Jebusites who lived in Jerusalem; so the Jebusites have lived there among the Benjaminites to this day.
The house of Joseph also went up against Bethel, and the LORD was with them.

versions.text: The house of Joseph also went up, against Bethel, and the LORD was with them.
versions.explanation: The comma after "up" wrongly separates the verb from its object and breaks the rhythm when read aloud.

text: They sent men to scout out Bethel, which was formerly called Luz.
The scouts saw a man coming out of the city and said to him, "Show us the way into the city, and we will treat you kindly."
So he showed them the way in, and they put the city to the sword, but they let the man and his whole family go.
The man went to the land of the Hittites, where he built a city and named it Luz; that is its name to this day.

Manasseh did not drive out the people of Beth-shean and its villages, or Taanach and its villages, or the people of Dor and its villages, or the people of Ibleam and its villages, or the people of Megiddo and its villages; the Canaanites were determined to remain in that land.
When Israel grew strong, they put the Canaanites to forced labor, but they never drove them out completely.
Ephraim did not drive out the Canaanites living in Gezer, so the Canaanites went on living there among them.
Zebulun did not drive out the people of Kitron or the people of Nahalol, so the Canaanites lived among them, but they were put to forced labor.
Asher did not drive out the people of Acco or Sidon, or of Ahlab, Achzib, Helbah, Aphik, or Rehob.
So the Asherites lived among the Canaanite inhabitants of the land, because they did not drive them out.

Naphtali did not drive out the people of Beth-shemesh or of Beth-anath, so they lived among the Canaanite inhabitants of the land; but the people of Beth-shemesh and Beth-anath were put to forced labor for them.
The Amorites pressed the Danites back into the hill country and would not let them come down into the plain.
The Amorites were determined to remain in Mount Heres, in Aijalon, and in Shaalbim, but as the house of Joseph grew stronger, they too were put to forced labor.
The territory of the Amorites ran from the Ascent of Akrabbim, from Sela on upward.

versions.text: The territory of the Amorites extended from the Ascent of Akrabbim to Sela and beyond.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew has two parallel phrases beginning with "from" (מִמַּעֲלֵה ... מֵהַסֶּלַע), not "from ... to"; the current rendering makes Sela the endpoint rather than a second reference point.
